messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a ~10% p99 bump on host-side tails after yesterday's kernel-picker changes. Repro on canary pods, only when requests hit the pretokenizer hot path. link: https://perf/redwood/1747 :eyes:

josh: ugh. is this the kernel affinity change?

maria: yeah, kernel selection now biases E-opt for short seqs. latency graphs show spikes correlate with high kv-cache churn.

kai: can you paste the flame? also which workload? small chat vs long-context?

maria: flame attached (short). workload = many short bursts (PLG demo). Key bits: host parse + streaming chunking stalled while kernel swap completes.

ranjit: if kvcache miss rate increases, we pay for extra parse + decode warmup. could be allocator churn too.

maria: profiler snapshot:
```
host_preparse  48%
kv_cache_lock  12%
kernel_select  9%
grpc_writev    7%
tokenizer      6%
```

josh: grpc_writev at 7% stands out — any change in HTTP/gRPC framing or batch size?

maria: not in prod config. but the new batching heuristics change request pacing; more micro-writes observed.

bench-bot: perf-run 1747201200 completed. summary: p99 +12% (short), p50 +2%. artifact: s3://bench/1747201200.tar.gz

kai: theory: kernel-picker making more frequent kernel swaps for short sequences which deopt KV cache locality -> more small writes -> grpc syscall overhead.

ranjit: possible mitigation: prefer stable kernel for requests with recent K/V hits; add a hysteresis window in selector. or prefer E-opt only after N consecutive short requests.

josh: can we simulate with rigged kv-hit patterns? i can run a replay with hot kv affinity pinned.

maria: tried pinning K/V affinity in canary, p99 back down ~3%. so kvcache locality is definitely a factor.

kai: also check tokenization path: we increased prefix normalization which adds memcpy for short tokens -> extra syscalls when combined with streaming chunking. small tokens + small chunks = many writes.

maria: agreeing. example snippet from logs: `STREAM_CHUNK: size=128, writev_count=3` repeated per request.

josh: action items?
- add hysteresis to kernel-picker (ranjit)
- reduce microwrites by coalescing small stream fragments (kai)
- run replay with kv-affinity pinned (josh)
- add a lightweight kvcache instrumentation flag to watch miss patterns (maria)

ranjit: i'll draft the hysteresis patch. tentative: require 2 consecutive kernel hints before switching, and a 200ms cooldown after swap.

kai: i'll try improving stream coalescer to hold tiny fragments for up to 4ms or until 1kB threshold. might affect tail, will canary.

maria: ran quick canary with hysteresis (local). p99 dropped ~6% compared to broken canary, but still +4% vs baseline. next run with coalescing + pinned kv looks promising.

bench-bot: scheduled full-run 1747203000 (coalesce + hysteresis). will post results.

josh: also log-level change: add a kvcache tag to each incoming request so we can tie misses to kernel decisions in trace. minimal overhead.

maria: agreed. will add tag and ship small PR. PR: https://gith/repo/pulls/5123

ranjit: quick question — do we need to adjust quantization kernels selection? might be unrelated but worth checking.

kai: leave quant kernels alone for now; focus host-side parse + stream coalesce. quant path didn't change in this rollout.

maria: follow-up: if coalescing + hysteresis reduces microwrites, grpc_writev cost should drop and kvcache locality should recover. if not, we'll revert kernel-picker changes.

josh: thx. ping me when bench-bot posts results.

ops-bot: deploy canary 1747203300 -> eng-runtime-canary-3 started by maria

bench-bot: run 1747203000 complete: p99 +1% (short), p50 +1%. artifacts: s3://bench/1747203000.tar.gz

maria: nice — that's within noise. looks like combined fix did the trick. rolling patch to canary -> prod after one more sanity run. :thumbsup:

kai: will open follow-up to tune coalescing thresholds based on real traffic.

ranjit: i'll land hysteresis patch in next hour.

josh: closing loop: add a test that simulates repeated short requests to prevent regression in future kernel-picker changes.

maria: noted. will add to perf suite. thanks all.
